newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Major loses another vote in upper house.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Major loses another vote in upper house.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives suffered a defeat in a vote in the upper House of Lords for the second successive day on Tuesday, adding to Prime Minister John Major's problems in pushing legislation through parliament.
But the defeat, on an amendment to a bill designed to crack down on the ownership of handguns following the Dunblane massacre, does not directly threaten Major's hold on power.
Major, with his party lagging the Labour opposition by 20 percentage points in opinion polls, is struggling to keep his government afloat until May when he must call a general election.
The main threat to his ability to do so is in the House of Commons (lower house) where he can no longer command an overall majority.
But the unelected upper chamber has this week also turned against him despite its large Conservative majority.

On Monday night, peers carried two opposition amendments to a bill that would have given police strong powers to counter organised crime by bugging suspects. The peers want to strengthen safeguards against abuse by insisting on prior approval by judges.
On Tuesday, the Lords voted by 158 to 135 for compensation for gun clubs affected by the clampdown on handguns.

The government, responding to public outrage over gunman Thomas Hamilton who shot dead 15 primary school children and a teacher in March last year, has brought in legislation to ban most handguns and make gun clubs tighten security.
But the gun lobby has accused it of over-reacting.
The government could seek to overturn the Lords' amendments when the two bills are discussed by the Commons.
But with feeling among its own supporters running high on both issues, it may be reluctant to risk humiliating defeats in the elected chamber.
